newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk deputies' probe clears Ciller of graft charge.
newsitem.headline: Turk deputies' probe clears Ciller of graft charge.

text.p: A Turkish parliamentary commission on Wednesday cleared Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller of the last of three corruption charges against her, commission member Sabri Ergul said.

"Like every time in the past, there was the well-known eight to seven vote and the proposal to send Ciller to the Supreme Court was rejected," opposition deputy Ergul told reporters after a meeting of the commission.

The 15-member commission, in which the government had a majority of one, was investigating Ciller's substantial personal wealth for signs of ill-gotten gains during her three years as prime minister from 1993.

It was the third corruption investigation against Ciller, who joined a coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan last June -- something she had vowed she would never do until the corruption allegations emerged.

A commission in November rejected a bid to send Ciller, now also foreign minister, to the Supreme Court over allegations she interfered in the sale of state-owned car manufacturer TOFAS to help business allies. Earlier in November she was cleared of failing to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company.
